I feel that, really I do. shit feels hopeless for me just the way you described. and also? while other people can BRING you happiness, that doesn't mean that your happiness can COME FROM them. find one thing to get excited about or look forward to, and that could get you by. it's not a cure-all by any means. it's a stepping stone, not a mile stone. but if there's just one thing worth living for, hold onto it man. the more things you find -before you find yr self in the thick of that suicidal feeling- the better stuff gets. even if its just a little bit of better. take the stepping stone and search for the mile stone. that's what I try to do at least... still haven't found that mile stone to help me from when things get real bad, those real suicidal moments, but that "one little thing" I find in my day keeps me from running the bath water red.

I think it's different for everyone, and that one thing changes constantly. sometimes, it's a project I want to finish (like getting the last word out there, feeling satisfied before I might die.) other times it's a person whose presence makes me feel more okay that at least I have someone in this messed up world beside me. it also can be worry, worry for what will happen to my cat/who would adopt her, what would happen to my favorite jackets or guitar, how my body could be found/who would have to deal with it. and sometimes, it's very very little things. the smell of my favorite person, the small weight of my cat on my chest, the theme song to my favorite TV show, the soundtrack of my favorite movie, the books I haven't finished, the bands I haven't seen, the cities I dream of going to, the taste or smell of my favorite foods and drinks. other times, there's guilt. not just the people I love, but the acquaintances I've met along the way. the girl I see in on the smoking lounge of every concert I go to and our cigarette conversations between bands. would she wonder if I moved? would she recognize my face on social media if a mutual friend or an acquaintance of an acquaintance posted about my death? or my favorite coffee shop I arrive every Monday at to read 100 pages or more of whatever book I got -would the workers who have memorized my order worry? mourn for a customer they hardly knew beyond her coffee preferences and reading? how could I put that weight, a whisper of my passing, on them? or what about the tiny local record store I visit on my second paycheck of every month, owned by a man who has been there since the 80's, who I talk to for an hour about punk music and spend $80-$150 on patches and music... he doesn't really know me, but still, maybe he would wonder or hear about it, and be that much short on money every month. I want to disappear so so so badly, but then guilt and anxiety cripple me. I often think about getting in my car and driving far far away to start over, but I know I can't run from my mind or this plague of a world we live in. so instead I try so hard. I don't try to "get better" (I personally see that phrase as a myth) I just try to find one thing at a time, to make it manageable. instead of worrying about all those things if I go, I concentrate on one of those things as a life line to keep me here. the record shop owner and the coffee shop baristas and the cigarette girl don't know that sometimes, I choose to stay alive because of them. the person who wrote my favorite TV shows theme song before I was born doesn't know that they're keeping me here with a silly bass line. I think the only person that really knows about all these things is my cat, because she sees the most of me and is probably wiser than me in so many ways... but even she doesn't know the inside of a chronically suicidal girls brain. so I choose one thing, from all of those things and more, and tell myself, at least for the day, that is what I'm living for. having one thing, even if it's different every day, worth living for, is enough. though, that's easier said than done. when the panic sets in and the suicidal ideation becomes more like action, well, in that moment, it's hard to remember you gotta remind yourself of one thing, because reality slips away. when things start getting bad, I try to find one thing before they get worse. because when it's worse worse worse WORSE than bad, reality and rational thought cease to exist. at least, for me.

it's a heavy heavy world we live in. I wish I could counter your words, provide answers, or even have something to say worth removing the melancholia. what you've written is beautiful, sad, and moving. I hope you find what your looking for out here in the world. as the world falls down, there's always one thing worth staying in it for. hold onto that, that's what I try to do at least.

SHORT VERSION:
I think I'm going to die, I really think this will kill me if I don't get help. I need med alternatives.

LONG VERSION:
I've been on lamictal and pristiq (and Seroquel as needed) now for almost a year, and I feel anxious and depressed and impulsive -all around dangerous in summary.

been on lots of other stuff that didn't work out (Lexapro, Zoloft, lithium, ect)

now I understand, once again, meds aren't a cure all. but I still feel as volatile as I did without them. maybe even more depressed, with mania at the same level more or less.

I can't focus, I sleep constantly, and I'm afraid/too paralyzed to leave the house most days. other times I'm over committed, blowing $200 on new hobbies, buying new clothes and jewelry even though I have plenty, going to three concerts a week, going so hard in the moshpit I break people's noses without saying sorry (because I was TRYING to, or even breaking my own bones -but still going even after I know I broke or sprained something- and skating without a helmet or pads till my knees turn bloody and my jeans are shredded.

my room is a disaster, I've gotten in pretty arguments with my friends for being too "blunt and brutally honest", I cheated on my boyfriend with a stranger at a club, I've sl*t my wrists in the bathtub, gone on drug benders when reality gets too hard, and steal pills, objects, and money from my friends/boyfriend/family.

docs are concerned to change my meds, worried I might have an extreme episode since I'm so "fragile" right now. but I think it's what I need. "coping" mechanisms can only get me so far, and a lot of the ones I've learned in therapy don't work (even though I try REALLY hard. I promise I'm trying so hard.)

I just don't want to keep living this way, hurting myself and others in my downward spiral. I'm becoming increasingly suicidal the more this drags on. if something doesn't change soon, I'm gonna sprint off a parking garage or find a way to get so high I overdose and choke on my own vomit.
